findings.shape: A mounded assembly of 180 thin curled flabellae connects to a branched base; the old floating disc and the rejected initial forest of separate stalks are replaced.
findings.surface: Warm cream/buff original numerical pigment and crinkled thin surfaces replace generic spherical florets. Fold relief is geometric rather than a photographic texture.
findings.movement: The same nonmotile folded body remains fixed with an optional enlarged drift overlay from selected fertile surface regions. No fruitbody growth, decomposition or air-current solver.
findings.evidenceScope: Actual Bergsma focus-stacked photograph compared with selected sensu-lato morphology and taxonomic clarification text. The focus stack is an authentic photographic technique, not a measured3D specimen. Regional narrow species limits are not independently resolved.
corrections: Replaced conspicuous parallel stalks with connected branching and densely curled thin folds.
Lowered peripheral folds to make a mound; merged retained rigid relief for performance.
Corrected the underside camera so the contextual pedestal no longer blocks this low body.
findings.residual: Folds remain too regular, pointed and ribbon-like in places; the underside branch fan is simplified. Natural frond edge lobing, tissue translucency, developmental branching, dimensions and species-complex variation remain incomplete.

limits: Partly stylized, unmeasured original educational reconstructions. Fine anatomy, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and physiology remain incomplete. Enlarged spore dots are a teaching overlay with authored timing, not measured release, Buller-drop mechanics or an airflow solver. No independent specialist validation, scientific certification or accuracy percentage.
